paragraphs.text: Zohar I 48a (Bereshit): "But on Shabbat the shelter of peace is spread over the world... and therefore in the sanctification of the day we bless, 'Who spreads the shelter of peace over us, over all His people Israel, and over Jerusalem.'" The Zohar continues (78:194): "Why 'over Jerusalem'? Because this is the dwelling place of that shelter." This is the basis for his opening: on Shabbat all Israel merit the holiness of Yerushalayim and the Mikdash.

The liturgy itself joins the Shabbat shelter to Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 69:7: "Another interpretation: this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Yaakov the Beit HaMikdash built, destroyed and built again... 'How awesome is this place' — this is the Temple built... 'This is none other' — this is the Temple destroyed, as it is said, 'For this our heart is faint' (Eichah 5:17)... 'but the house of God' — built and perfected in the time to come, as it is said, 'For He has strengthened the bars of your gates.'" The Sefaria text attaches 'built and perfected' to 'the house of God'; in the discussion “House of Elokim and the Gate of Heaven,” Rav Tzadok rejects that reading and attaches it to 'this is the gate of heaven', with the Matnos Kehunah and the Yalkut.

The passage stands at the end of 26a, as he says; it speaks of the dried river flowing again when Israel leaves exile, which fits the rebuilt Temple.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Peri Tzadik, Rosh Hashanah 8 (Rav Tzadok): the same teaching almost word for word: "the great, the mighty and the awesome" correspond to the three Avos, and Yaakov is "awesome," since fear falls on him from Hashem "without his own effort," while Yitzchak's fear comes from picturing that the King of kings stands over him; it also uses Pesachim 88a (Yaakov called it "house", permanence). It adds that this is why "And so, place Your fear" (Uvechen ten pachdecha) is said in the blessing Atah Kadosh, which corresponds to Yaakov.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 69b: "Yirmiyahu came and said: Foreigners are shrieking in His sanctuary — where are His awesome deeds? He did not say 'awesome.' Daniel came and said: Foreigners are enslaving His children — where are His mighty deeds? He did not say 'mighty.' They came and said: On the contrary, this is the might of His might, that He conquers His inclination... And these are His awesome deeds: were it not for the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, how could one nation survive among the nations?" (69b:14–15). Yirmiyahu dropped 'awesome' because foreigners were shrieking in the Temple; the Men of the Great Assembly restored it: Israel's survival shows God's awe.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 6:1: “This is the meaning of the holy Zohar cited above, that the good inclination, the holy Matronita, the Kingship of holiness, descends on Shabbat: for yetzer means desire, as it is said, ‘Keep this forever as the yetzer of the thoughts of the heart of Your people.’ When King David, peace be upon him, saw then how they had given with a willing heart and with great desire, he asked of Hashem, ‘Keep this forever as the yetzer,’ and so forth: that the desire Israel had should remain forever. paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shevat 2:1: “We have already explained that yetzer means desire, as in ‘the yetzer of the thoughts of the heart of Your people.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, created desire to be a longing for Torah, as it will be in the time to come (as written in Zohar I 138a); only ‘you make it evil.’ Concerning this they said (Kiddushin 30b): ‘I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its spice,’ and they said, ‘If this repulsive one meets you, drag him to the study hall’ — that is, the desire and the yetzer are to be for the study hall, to become the joy of Torah learning. If so, only one yetzer was created; how then does it say that the Holy One, blessed be He, created two? Rather, this refers to the two chambers of the heart... And concerning this: the bent Tzadi, the bent righteous man — to be mighty, the one who conquers his inclination, ‘drag him to the study hall’; that is ‘bent,’ to bend his inclination with might and make it good, so that all worldly matters are in holiness.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, Yoma 69b: “It appears that they certainly do not disagree; rather, each of them added or omitted among His powers and titles according to what he saw, in his own time, of the ability and powers of the Holy One, blessed be He... Yirmiyahu came and saw in his generation and his time idolaters dancing in His sanctuary, and said, ‘Where are His awesome deeds?’ and therefore omitted ‘the awesome.’ This was at the beginning of the exile, at the destruction of the Temple, when Israel was not yet enslaved to the idolaters, so he still said ‘the mighty’ — until Daniel came, who was in Babylon in exile and saw the enslavement of exile, and therefore said, ‘Where are His mighty deeds?’ and omitted ‘the mighty.’ ... Until the Men of the Great Assembly came, who lived at the end of the seventy years of the Babylonian exile and saw that in those years Israel was saved from many troubles, such as the episode of Haman, from which they were saved through Mordechai, who was one of the Great Assembly. They returned to say: in all these years in which the Holy One, blessed be He, was patient with the wicked, this is His might, that He conquers His inclination; and this is His awe, that one nation, and so forth — as they said, ‘one sheep among seventy wolves.’”

h: House of Elokim and the Gate of Heaven

p: — And this is the depth of the words of
— the question of the holy Zohar
— "'This stone shall be the house of God' (Bereishis 28:22) —
— it should have said 'the house of Hashem,'
— 'Let us go to the house of Hashem,' etc." (Tehillim 122:1).
— So too the Midrash Rabbah was troubled:
אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם בֵּית ה'.
— "this is none other than the house of Hashem."
— that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed
— and then it is called "the house of Hashem,"
— that the dread of Hashem and the fear fall
— it is not manifest that it is awesome,
— that the dread of Hashem falls
— since they shriek in His sanctuary;
— and then it is not called "the house of Hashem"
— the dread of Hashem from the Beit HaMikdash,
— the Men of the Great Assembly:
— "and this is the gate of heaven" —
— and on this the Midrash Rabbah brings:
— 'For He has strengthened the bars of your gates,'"
— Rather, the main point is that it expounded
— "and this is the gate of heaven"
— as referring to the Temple built and perfected

h: Shabbat, the Well and the River from Eden

p: — And regarding Shabbat it is written:
— and to visit in His sanctuary" (Tehillim 27:4);
— for then Hashem, may He be blessed,
— spreads the shelter of peace over us, etc.,
— and this comes through the attribute of
— Yaakov our forefather, peace be upon him.
— And this is what is said of Yaakov:
— "And he looked, and behold, a well in the field,"
— the level of "the Lord of all the earth,"
— As written in the holy Zohar
— that Yaakov is the supernal chariot,
— from the spring of all springs —
— as written in the holy Zohar;
— And of Moshe it is written:
— the image of the central pillar
— Rather, he was from the inside —
— and that one from the soul."
— That is, Moshe is the soul,
— Therefore it is written of him,
— for he was "the man of God,"
— and the Holy One, blessed be He,
— as it were, would fulfill it.
— And it is mentioned seven times,
— indicating that he is in wholeness,
— that he radiates to Knesses Yisrael
— And this is the attribute of "awesome":
— so that it enters the depths of the heart.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Peri Tzadik, Tetzaveh 12 (Rav Tzadok): also about Shabbat: "immediately at the entry of Shabbat the dread and the fear fall upon him", with the Shabbat-night meal set against Yitzchak and fear that comes "when he sees that the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, stands over him" (the Rema’s wording quoted above in the contrast between Yitzchak’s fear and Yaakov’s awe). paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, V'Zot HaBerachah 2:1: "'Moshe, the man of God'... Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Were it not a written verse, it would be impossible to say it: just as a man decrees upon his wife and she does it, so the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed upon Moshe and he did it for Him." The printed text reverses the roles out of reverence (see the Sefaria translator's note there); the sense, as the author reads it, is that Moshe decreed and God fulfilled. The exact words 'and Moshe would decree and the Holy One, blessed be He, would fulfill' appear in Midrash Tanchuma, Vaera 3:2.
